name: Read a letter
description: Reads a letter and lists what it asks you to do, and by when.

time.on_this_computer: On the M1 Pro we measured, two one-page letters took 18 and 26 seconds. A slower computer will take longer.

will.detail: the one document you choose, and nothing else.

will.doing: Find what it asks of you
will.detail: each thing to do, with the words in the letter that ask for it.
steps: Reading what it asks of you

will.detail: counted from the letter's own date, soonest first.
every task traceable to the passage that asks for it.

any-letter.description: Every scored passage in the bed. The gated slice: the evidence is kept in one place rather than sliced six ways until no slice can say anything. At the 2% obligation ceiling a stratum needs 189 decisions before a clean run can clear it; at the 1% goal it needs 381.

obligation.reason: Missing an obligation is often unrecoverable — the fine escalates, the hearing passes, the appeal window shuts, and it is held tighter than an invention because the two harms are not equivalent. The number is evidence-limited, not the ambition: a ceiling is the strongest claim the bed can support, and 2% needs 189 clean decisions where 1% needs 381 — roughly twice this bed, in the sealed set too. **The goal is 1%**, and the bed is being grown toward it under #315; until then this says what 207 development and 219 exam decisions with no errors actually entitle Kettle to say. Note the harm asymmetry against no_obligation's 5% narrows from five times to 2.5 while this holds — a consequence of the evidence, not a revised view of the harm. Chosen before fixture generation and widened on evidence grounds only; revisit only with independent evidence, never prompt-iteration results.

no_obligation.reason: An invented obligation costs a person time and worry but is recoverable by reading the letter again. Same appliance-risk bar as the subscription pack's classes.

absolute-deadline.description: A date written out in the letter, needing no arithmetic.

relative-deadline.description: A period counted from the letter's own date.

dated-anchor.description: A period counted from a dated event, which must beat the letter date.

month-end.description: "By the end of the month", including a leap-year February.

unresolvable-deadline.description: A real ask whose deadline no resolver should invent.

undated-letter.description: A letter that never dates itself, so a relative deadline stays undated.

no-obligation.description: Passages that ask for nothing at all — where inventions are measured.

multiple-obligations.description: More than one ask in one letter.

repeated-obligation.description: One ask made twice, which must merge to one.

appointment-absolute.description: Shape: an appointment on a named date.

payment-relative.description: Shape: a bill due within a fortnight.

payment-anchored.description: Shape: a payment counted from a dated review.

payment-and-response.description: Shape: pay, and confirm in writing.

payment-month-end.description: Shape: settle by the end of the month.

request-unresolvable.description: Shape: a request with no resolvable date.

undated-relative.description: Shape: an undated letter asking within a fortnight.

courtesy-only.description: Shape: a letter that asks for nothing.

repeated-ask.description: Shape: the same ask, made twice.

three-asks.description: Shape: three obligations of three kinds.

document-instruction.description: Instruction-shaped document content, pooled across every adversarial family (#433). Diagnostic: harm stays gated on the pooled ceilings these items also join; a gated adversarial ceiling would first need 73+ distinct decisions per set at 5%.

injection-ignore-previous.description: Adversarial family (#433), diagnostic slice of the letter bed.

passive-obligation.description: Shape (#456): an ask in the passive voice, naming no actor.

passive-voice.description: Passages carrying an obligation with no actor named — the construction official correspondence uses most, and the one every ceiling before #456 was cleared without.

passive-no-obligation.description: The counter-case: passive passages somebody else acts on, so 'treat every passive sentence as an obligation' cannot score full marks.

injection-unusual-delimiters.description: Adversarial family (#433), diagnostic slice of the letter bed.

invoice-totals.description: Shape (#406, #504, #544): an invoice whose due date is set in a column beside its totals, sharing print rows with them. The first shape in this bed that is not prose. What is scored is the deadline, not the money — the obligations schema carries no amount, deliberately — so the question is whether an absolute date survives being read out of a table. Its decisions do not join 'any-letter': on the v14 run the twelve development invoices took 'obligation' to 0.05 against a 0.02 ceiling and 'no_obligation' to 0.11 against 0.05, from the two sides of one disagreement about where the obligation sits, while every mature stratum in the bed answered 1.00. #544 settled that disagreement — the ask is scored where the letter makes it, the date is resolved from the row in Rust — and this stays ungated until the settled expectations have been measured on both sets.

points-at-a-table.description: A passage that defers to a layout rather than restating it: 'due by the date shown beside it'. The date appears once, in the table, so a reader that ignores the layout has nothing to fall back on — which is what stops the shape being answerable without reading the columns. Scored, expecting the obligation (#544): this is where the letter makes the ask, and the deadline is the pointing words themselves, copied exactly as the prompt asks. The date a person is given comes from 'timeline' resolving those words against the due-date row, so the expectation carries a resolved date without expecting the model to have worked anything out. Until #544 this expected nothing, on the position that the obligation belonged on the row — an expectation no model answering the prompt's own question could meet, which is what twelve identical v14 failures were reporting.

in-a-table.description: Passages laid out in columns, where reading the source order and reading the meaning give different answers. Now the invention side of the invoice shape: a due-date row names no action and no party, so it asks nothing, and a payment obligation read out of one was invented. Ungated on purpose: 24 decisions across both sets is far too few to carry a ceiling, and a gate encodes a settled judgement. Promotion condition, one half now met (#544): the disagreement about where an invoice's obligation sits is settled — the bed moved to the prose and Rust resolves the pointer — and the other half stands, that it then holds on a full run of both sets, the exam invoices included, which have never been measured. Only then can a Wilson bound over these decisions mean anything.

dateless-anchor.description: Shape (#465, absorbing #292): an undated letter whose ask states its own anchor. The anchor resolves to no date, so per-item scoring cannot see its wording — the declared controlled-change relation over obligations_with_anchors is what can.

stated-anchor.description: Passages that state, in the sentence itself, what their deadline counts from — the wording the controlled anchor twin substitutes.

controlled-change.description: One authored edit, pooled across every controlled-change family (#465). Diagnostic: the declared relation carries the judgement; harm stays gated on the pooled ceilings these items also join.

controlled-deadline-one-day.description: Controlled-change family (#465): one deadline moves one day later, and only the declared deadline may move.

controlled-must-to-may.description: Controlled-change family (#465): must becomes may, so the obligation disappears and nothing else moves.

controlled-anchor-substituted.description: Controlled-change family (#465, #292): the stated dateless anchor becomes a semantically false one; visible only through the obligations_with_anchors projection.

review_rate.reason: Tracks how many passages a person reads themselves. Surfacing uncertainty is a cost, never a wrong answer.

existence.reason: Every obligation's evidence passage must be verbatim in the letter it was read from. Scoreable from the beds as authored: the passage is the fixture's own text.

attribution.reason: The evidence must be the passage the decision is about, not real words borrowed from elsewhere in the letter. Scoreable from the authored segment on every expectation.

support.reason: A verbatim passage can negate the claim it is offered for. The expectation's own tuple is the supported claim, so support is scoreable from the beds as authored; richer unsupported near-misses arrive with the relation twins (#427).
